report.summary: I made the one bounded fix to generated/hello-world.mjs that the admitted baseline failure justified. That baseline is observation result://abiogenesis/7d8d7f5f… on CLI bytes sha256:647697a5…. In it, `node generated/hello-world.mjs` exited 0 but printed "Hello world!\n" with no comma, and `node --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs` exited 1 with pass 0 and fail 2. Both strictEqual assertions failed on the missing comma. I changed `console.log("Hello world!");` to `console.log("Hello, world!");`, and the CLI's digest is now sha256:fe8f40803a256b5b65c97f5f4cae862fd55b37cb81f2a803c56c3f654c22e9ef. The baseline failure stays historical evidence about the old bytes 647697a5…; I did not re-target it to the new bytes. I ran both fixed commands myself only as a check; this is not admitted evidence or acceptance. The CLI printed exactly "Hello, world!\n" (14 bytes) with exit 0, and the test run exited 0 with tests 2, pass 2, fail 0. I changed no other files. The original source (ce602ce2…), oracle (028073e4…), witness contract (f97359de…), component test (8b55bf3f…) and UAT test (5449c227…) still hash to their admitted values. The fix needs no package, install or network access.
